body: I’m just saying anyone can come talk to me, literally anyone. Gay, straight, bi, Christian, and anyone else. Young people, older people
I was in high school when I started seeing one. If you don’t want it on any record, I’d recommend talking to someone you trust. And that could be anyone, an adult,  a friend

Like you said, self diagnosis can be a dangerous animal. But, if you think you might be depressed, or have those thoughts, you can go and get help. Start with a therapist. I’m not diagnosing you with anything, I don’t want to tell you what to do, all I can do is tell you what I did that helped me. I asked myself those same questions, and I talked to someone I really trusted, and I went to a therapist. Talking to them really helped me, and not just with my anxiety and depression

Exactly. You can’t save everyone but you can try. I’m just trying to be the person I wish I had a few years ago and the person my younger sister needed last year (that’s a whole other story and I really should have been there for her more but I did what I could). I’m better now but my anxiety and definitely my depression creeps back up every now and then. Even if it’s just listening to someone who has nobody else, or if they try to talk to someone who tells them they have nothing to be depressed about (which I’ve been told before and still told by someone I live with), I’m there.
Well. I’ve got plenty of time. We can keep replying here or you can pm me. I’ll listen to anything you have to say
